raw_graphql_pull_request.body: ## Motivation TL;DR make post-processing of log lines be more accurate by inserting log lines even when server is idle. This is controlled by `SGLANG_LOG_IDLE_BATCH_STATS`, off by default which maintains previous behavior. Without idle logs, stats that can vary within the idle time (e.g., #transfer-req) is not visible. Furthermore, it is not possible to infer how large a time window a log line covers. Before PR: After PR: PD prefill and decode workers log a `Prefill batch` / `Decode batch` line only for forwards that do work. A worker with no forward to run, or such an attention-DP rank, prints nothing, though it can be in either of two states: 1. **Idle**: no requests exist. 2. **Blocked**: requests exist but wait on something other than compute. With the defaults (`early` decode allocation, no optimistic prefill), prefill starts a request only after decode has reserved KV cache for it. While the decode KV pool is full, new requests wait in the prefill bootstrap queue and the prefill worker has nothing to run. Such waiting is worth observing because acting on it pays off. `--disaggregation-decode-allocation-policy prefill_complete` (#40703) reserves decode KV only after prefill, so requests compute instead of waiting for a decode slot; #45337 extends it to PP prefill and reports larger decode batches and higher throughput. Without this change, the logs show nothing in either state, and with `--enable-metrics` the Prometheus queue gauges refresh only every 30 s while idle. With it, the idle lines keep reporting `#bootstrap-req` (prefill) and `#prealloc-req` / `#transfer-req` (decode), so the logs show which state a worker is in and how long requests waited. Line timing is the other half. Each line stands for the time since the previous line of its rank. Without lines while idle, any average over log lines over-weights busy periods, and analysis cannot tell idle time from missing data. Without a line right before the forward that ends an idle stretch, the first busy line's window also covers the idle time before it, which dilutes its throughput (see the sample below). Decode lines of attention-DP ranks also land on different forwards, because a rank does not count the idle forwards it runs in lockstep with busy peers. That makes it hard to match lines across ranks. Example: a prefill worker busy for 1 s with 3 queued requests, then idle for 1 s. The mean `#queue-req` over its lines is 3.0 today; with this change it is about 1.5, the time average. ### Sample logs One prefill and one decode worker on one GB300 node: Qwen3-8B with dummy weights, TP1 each, Mooncake, `SGLANG_LOG_MS=1`. Decode runs with `--max-total-tokens 40000`, so its KV pool fills up. The same client ran with the flag off and on: 4 long requests fill the decode KV pool, and 8 more arrive 3 s later and wait for decode KV. Lines are cut to the relevant fields; `#` lines are annotations. **Prefill, before** (flag off). Prefill logs nothing for 6 s, including 3.6 s while 8 requests wait in its bootstrap queue. The first line after the gap reports 1295 token/s, because its window includes the gap. ``` [2026-10-28 00:47:24.245] Prefill batch, #new-seq: 1, #new-token: 1, #bootstrap-req: 0, #inflight-req: 1, input throughput (token/s): 0.38 # 00:47:45.998 client starts and sends nothing for 6 s # 00:47:52.019 client: 4 requests arrive (8000 input tokens, 1500 output tokens each) [2026-10-28 00:47:52.208] Prefill batch, #new-seq: 1, #new-token: 8000, #bootstrap-req: 0, #inflight-req: 1, input throughput (token/s): 286.09 [2026-10-28 00:47:52.372] Prefill batch, #new-seq: 3, #new-token: 16384, #bootstrap-req: 0, #inflight-req: 3, input throughput (token/s): 99826.98 [2026-10-28 00:47:52.441] Prefill batch, #new-seq: 1, #new-token: 7616, #bootstrap-req: 0, #inflight-req: 4, input throughput (token/s): 109946.76 # 00:47:55.032 client: 8 more requests arrive; the decode KV pool is full [2026-10-28 00:47:58.617] Prefill batch, #new-seq: 1, #new-token: 8000, #bootstrap-req: 5, #inflight-req: 1, input throughput (token/s): 1295.42 ``` **Prefill, after** (flag on). Idle lines report `#bootstrap-req: 0` while no requests exist, then `#bootstrap-req: 8` while requests wait for decode KV. The line right before each forward that ends an idle stretch (`#bootstrap-req: 3` and `7`) bounds the next batch line's window to that forward, which then reports 52,648 and 85,425 token/s. ``` # 00:44:10.701 client starts and sends nothing for 6 s [2026-10-28 00:44:10.976] Prefill batch, #new-seq: 0, #new-token: 0, #bootstrap-req: 0, #inflight-req: 0, input throughput (token/s): 0.00 # ... 4 more lines like the one above [2026-10-28 00:44:15.976] Prefill batch, #new-seq: 0, #new-token: 0, #bootstrap-req: 0, #inflight-req: 0, input throughput (token/s): 0.00 # 00:44:16.702 client: 4 requests arrive (8000 input tokens, 1500 output tokens each) [2026-10-28 00:44:16.738] Prefill batch, #new-seq: 0, #new-token: 0, #bootstrap-req: 3, #inflight-req: 0, input throughput (token/s): 0.00 [2026-10-28 00:44:16.890] Prefill batch, #new-seq: 1, #new-token: 8000, #bootstrap-req: 0, #inflight-req: 1, input throughput (token/s): 52648.10 [2026-10-28 00:44:17.057] Prefill batch, #new-seq: 3, #new-token: 16384, #bootstrap-req: 0, #inflight-req: 3, input throughput (token/s): 98325.41 [2026-10-28 00:44:17.124] Prefill batch, #new-seq: 1, #new-token: 7616, #bootstrap-req: 0, #inflight-req: 4, input throughput (token/s): 113680.60 [2026-10-28 00:44:17.281] Prefill batch, #new-seq: 0, #new-token: 0, #bootstrap-req: 0, #inflight-req: 0, input throughput (token/s): 0.00 # ... 14 more lines like the one above [2026-10-28 00:44:19.631] Prefill batch, #new-seq: 0, #new-token: 0, #bootstrap-req: 0, #inflight-req: 0, input throughput (token/s): 0.00 # 00:44:19.715 client: 8 more requests arrive; the decode KV pool is full [2026-10-28 00:44:19.788] Prefill batch, #new-seq: 0, #new-token: 0, #bootstrap-req: 8, #inflight-req: 0, input throughput (token/s): 0.00 # ... 20 more lines like the one above [2026-10-28 00:44:23.079] Prefill batch, #new-seq: 0, #new-token: 0, #bootstrap-req: 8, #inflight-req: 0, input throughput (token/s): 0.00 [2026-10-28 00:44:23.209] Prefill batch, #new-seq: 0, #new-token: 0, #bootstrap-req: 7, #inflight-req: 0, input throughput (token/s): 0.00 [2026-10-28 00:44:23.303] Prefill batch, #new-seq: 1, #new-token: 8000, #bootstrap-req: 5, #inflight-req: 1, input throughput (token/s): 85424.88 ``` **Decode, before.** The last line reports 2 running requests and 8256 tokens; nothing follows while the worker is idle. ``` [2026-10-28 00:48:00.828] Decode batch, #running-req: 3, #token: 24768, #prealloc-req: 0, #transfer-req: 0, gen throughput (token/s): 863.54 [2026-10-28 00:48:00.981] Decode batch, #running-req: 2, #token: 8256, #prealloc-req: 0, #transfer-req: 0, gen throughput (token/s): 642.31 # no further decode lines ``` **Decode, after.** The first step without a forward closes the burst's tail with `#running-req: 0`, and idle lines follow. ``` [2026-10-28 00:44:25.516] Decode batch, #running-req: 3, #token: 24768, #prealloc-req: 0, #transfer-req: 0, gen throughput (token/s): 858.05 [2026-10-28 00:44:25.668] Decode batch, #running-req: 2, #token: 8256, #prealloc-req: 0, #transfer-req: 0, gen throughput (token/s): 648.44 [2026-10-28 00:44:25.751] Decode batch, #running-req: 0, #token: 0, #prealloc-req: 0, #transfer-req: 0, gen throughput (token/s): 291.84 [2026-10-28 00:44:25.909] Decode batch, #running-req: 0, #token: 0, #prealloc-req: 0, #transfer-req: 0, gen throughput (token/s): 0.00 # ... 35 more lines like the one above [2026-10-28 00:44:31.611] Decode batch, #running-req: 0, #token: 0, #prealloc-req: 0, #transfer-req: 0, gen throughput (token/s): 0.00 ``` ## Modifications New env var `SGLANG_LOG_IDLE_BATCH_STATS` (default off, PD prefill and decode workers only). The line format is unchanged. - **Idle-forward lines.** An attention-DP rank without work logs one prefill line per idle forward. On decode, idle forwards count toward `--decode-log-interval`, so every rank logs on the same forwards. A cache flush does not reset that count, since it reaches ranks at different forwards. - **Timed lines.** While no forward runs, a line is logged once no line has been logged for an EMA of the recent gap between forward-paced lines (1 s before one is measured). - **Idle boundaries.** A line is logged right before the forward that ends a stretch of timed lines (and before the first forward after startup); it reports no running requests, since none ran in its window. On decode, the first step without a forward closes the forwards since the previous line at once. An idle stretch long enough for a timed line therefore starts and ends at a line, and the first busy window after it holds only the forward, not the idle tail. - **Line windows.** Each line covers the time since the previous line of its rank: its throughput and, with `SGLANG_ENABLE_METRICS_DEVICE_TIMER`, its occupancy. - **Decode metrics with the flag on.** - Every decode line closes the window since the previous line and exports it, on ranks that log and on ranks that only export metrics. Decode gauges therefore stay current on idle attention-DP ranks and while the worker is idle. - Speculative acceptance gauges keep their last value through windows without speculative forwards. - `last_gen_throughput` (`/server_info`) keeps the last busy rate. When the worker goes idle, the `gen_throughput` gauge reads the rate of the last burst's tail, then 0. - `RECORD_STEP_TIME` records only windows of exactly `--decode-log-interval` forwards. The prefill and decode SoL hooks are not called for windows without work. - **Independent of the flag.** - Retract-mode `pause_generation` now zeroes the exported `gen_throughput` gauge. The paused loop skips idle housekeeping, so nothing else replaced the last rate. - A decode export of a batch whose requests all finished reports `decode_sum_seq_lens` 0 instead of the batch's stale `seq_lens`. With the flag off, logs and exports are unchanged apart from those two fixes. ## Accuracy Tests Not applicable: no change to model outputs. ## Speed Tests and Profiling Not benchmarked. With it on, an idle worker logs and exports about as often as a busy one, unless `--sleep-on-idle` is set. ## Validation - Unit tests on CPU: - `test_idle_batch_stats_lines.py`: 21 cases. That revision predates the decode window, Prometheus and idle boundary changes above. - This revision produced the sample logs above (one prefill and one decode rank, no attention DP). They show timed, idle-start and idle-end lines. Attention-DP alignment and the Prometheus changes are covered by unit tests only. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. A stretch with such lines also gets a line right before the forward that ends it (so does startup, before the first forward), and on decode the first step without a forward closes the forwards since the previous line, so the idle stretch starts and ends at a line. Idle lines thus come about as often as busy ones, and each line covers about the same wall time, so a plain average over the lines approximates a time average; weighting each line by the time since the previous line is more accurate. Every decode line closes the window since the previous line and exports it: decode Prometheus gauges and KV-event metrics are refreshed on every line, including on idle attention-DP ranks and while idle, and the gen_throughput gauge is the rate of that window. The line before a forward reports no running requests, since none ran in its window, and reads its queue gauges after that forward's requests were admitted. Speculative acceptance gauges keep their last value through windows without speculative forwards, and last_gen_throughput in /server_info keeps the rate of the last busy window. With SGLANG_ENABLE_METRICS_DEVICE_TIMER, each line's occupancy also covers the time since the previous line.
